title: Silas and the Songbook
premise: Ivo Zhou inherited her grandmother's failing orchard along with a tangle of debts and a deed that inexplicably lists a second name: Silas Marchetti, the boy who left town fifteen years ago and never wrote back. When Silas returns to claim his half, their uneasy co-custody of the orchard becomes an uneasy cohabitation as harvest season forces them together. Digging through her grandmother's songbook, Ivo uncovers letters proving the old woman deliberately bound them together to force a reconciliation neither wanted. In the end, Ivo must choose between selling the orchard to erase the past and keeping it—and Silas—choosing truth over the safe invisibility she built her life on.
about_author: Jonah Almeida is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories set in places where the work is hard and the silences are louder. They live in a converted packing house with too many instruments and one very opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A county clerk refuses to process Ivo's loan application because the orchard deed lists two names: hers and Silas Marchetti's. She drives home furious through autumn fog, cataloguing everything she's rebuilt in five careful years. Emotional beat: dread—the safe life she constructed has a crack running straight through it.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback woven with present: how her grandmother's death and the debts taught Ivo to live small—no risks, no attachments, last train always caught. Her best friend Priya pushes her to fight the deed legally instead of ignoring it. Emotional beat: resignation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas arrives with a duffel bag and a lawyer's letter, expecting a hostile empty property, and finds Ivo pruning in the rain. Their first conversation is all barbed politeness. He claims he only wants what's fair. Emotional beat: wary recognition—fifteen years haven't erased the shape of each other.

chapters.title: Terms of Occupation
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Forced by the deed's terms, they agree to split the orchard down the middle until probate resolves—one takes the house, one the bunkhouse. The negotiation is a duel disguised as paperwork. Emotional beat: grudging respect buried under grievance.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Working her half, Ivo finds trees grafted with two varieties side by side—her grandmother's signature trick—and remembers Silas's father teaching them both to graft as children. She says nothing when Silas notices. Emotional beat: grief surfacing where anger used to be.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Cleaning the bunkhouse, Silas discovers a battered songbook of folk tunes annotated in two hands—his mother's and Ivo's grandmother's. The margin notes stop abruptly fifteen years ago, the year everyone stopped speaking. Emotional beat: curiosity turning to unease about what really happened.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A storm knocks out power; Silas misses the last train into town and sleeps in the bunkhouse. Ivo lies awake listening to the rain, furious at how little his presence unsettles her. Emotional beat: the first involuntary softening.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A creditor arrives; Silas quietly covers a payment from savings he'd meant for his own fresh start, then lies about it. Ivo finds the receipt anyway. Emotional beat: guilt entangling loyalty—he's paying for sins he may not have committed.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Harvest begins understaffed; they fall into wordless working rhythm, passing crates and ladders like they never stopped. Priya observes that Ivo laughs more in a week than in five years. Emotional beat: warmth arriving without permission.

chapters.title: The Year Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pressured by Priya, Ivo finally asks why Silas left. His answer—his mother's illness, his father's disgrace, a town that chose sides—collides with her memory of being abandoned mid-summer. Both versions can't be true. Emotional beat: the central wound reopened.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Deciphering the songbook's margin notes, Silas realizes the two women were writing to each other across years—coded messages about the orchard, the feud, and two children they were determined to bind back together. Emotional beat: revelation—the estrangement was engineered, or at least exploited.

chapters.title: An Offer from Hollow Creek
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A developer offers enough to clear every debt and fund the life Ivo always denied herself—if both names sign. She wants to say yes before she examines why the offer feels like erasure. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as freedom.

chapters.title: What Silas Knew
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Confronted with the margin notes, Silas admits he found letters years ago proving his father's debt was manufactured by a rival—and stayed away out of shame, letting Ivo believe the worst. She walks out. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; the truth costs more than the lie.

chapters.title: Winter Pruning
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Weeks of silence; Ivo prunes alone and catches herself leaving half the work undone, waiting for hands that won't come. She rereads her grandmother's final letter and finds a line she'd never let herself read twice: 'Truth is just loyalty to someone who isn't in the room.' Emotional beat: the turn toward courage.

chapters.title: The Rival's Ledger
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Following the forged ledger trail together—first collaboration since the rupture—they trace the manufactured debt to the developer now making the offer. The rescue bid was a land grab all along. Emotional beat: alliance reforged in shared outrage.

chapters.title: Cider and Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the first frost night, Silas presses the last apples and confesses everything else: that he came back not for the deed but because the songbook's last entry named him, and he needed to know if anyone had waited. Ivo admits she kept his side of the grafting knife. Emotional beat: mutual exposure, tender and terrifying.

chapters.title: Sign Here
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The developer escalates with a deadline and legal threats; signing means safety, refusing means a fight they might lose. At the lawyer's office, pen hovering, Ivo sees the deed's fine print: the dual names were her grandmother's deliberate condition, revocable only by joint choice. Emotional beat: climax pressure—every door narrowing to one.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. Silas, believing Ivo will sell and wanting to spare her the cost of choosing him, packs to leave on the evening train. Ivo races the platform clock and asks him—not to stay for the orchard—but to stay and be chosen. Emotional beat: romantic climax; vulnerability as victory.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Ground
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They refuse the sale and file jointly against the developer, using the forged-ledger evidence. It will take months and money they don't have, but the town—stirred by the old scandal's truth—begins showing up with tractors and casseroles. Emotional beat: community as redemption.

chapters.title: Spring Grafting
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Planting season: they graft new stock using both families' varieties, finishing the pattern their elders started. Silas teaches Ivo's niece the knife work; Ivo watches and lets herself imagine permanence. Emotional beat: healing made physical, generational.

chapters.title: The Songbook Completed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the songbook's empty pages, Ivo and Silas write new entries—songs, notes, arguments, plans—continuing the correspondence their grandmothers began. The debts are restructured; the orchard survives lean but alive. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as something you add to, not merely receive.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing chapter. One year later: a small wedding under the grafted trees, the deed framed on the wall with both names inked over in the same hand. Ivo reflects that staying visible was the bravest harvest of all. Final image: the last train passes in the distance, and neither of them looks up. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy.
